Archetype.description:
Optional 'help me choose' path.

The primary way to name a component is its ARM resource type — that's what
people already know and it's unambiguous. An archetype is only for the case
where the service genuinely hasn't been chosen yet and the engine should
pick (e.g. Postgres Flexible Server vs Azure SQL DB vs SQL MI).
Archetype.title: Archetype

CapabilityClass.description:
Coarse compute classes, used as a pre-filter over real VM families.
Narrower needs go in `sku_hints`, which shrinks the qualifying pool.
CapabilityClass.title: CapabilityClass

CapacityRequest.description:
Declared compute demand.

Deliberately absent: any notion of reservation or savings-plan lock-in.
Azure savings plans apply across regions and families, so commitment is
effectively placement-neutral and doesn't belong in a placement decision.

sku_hints.description: Concrete VM SKUs, e.g. ['Standard_ND96isr_H100_v5']. Narrowing here shrinks the qualifying pool and lowers capacity confidence.
sku_hints.title: Sku Hints

growth.description: Expected growth over the workload's horizon, e.g. '3x/12mo'. Scored against projected demand, not just current.
growth.title: Growth

CapacityRequest.title: CapacityRequest

Component.description:
One deployable piece of the workload.

Named by ARM resource type wherever the service is already chosen — that is
the primary path. `archetype` is the optional alternative for when it isn't.

archetype.description: Used only when the concrete service hasn't been chosen yet.

capabilities.description: Per-region service capabilities this component needs — the level below 'is the service in the region', e.g. ['zone-redundant-ha', 'customer-managed-key']. Named after Azure's own `locations/{location}/capabilities` APIs, which is where most of these facts come from.
capabilities.title: Capabilities

residency.description: Override. Intersected with the workload and flow envelopes.

topology.description: Override for a standing mandate. Normally the engine derives this from the RTO/RPO of the flows this component serves.

required.description: False marks the component as droppable if it alone blocks a region.
required.title: Required

Component.title: Component

Criticality.description:
WAF RE:02 flow criticality rating. Drives what the engine sacrifices when
the constraints can't all be met.
Criticality.title: Criticality

DemandSource.description:
Where the users are. CAF's second region-selection step is proximity to
users; this is the input for it.

share.description: Fraction of total demand from this origin.
share.title: Share

latency_p99_ms.description: Target p99 round-trip from this origin. Scored, not enforced.
latency_p99_ms.title: Latency P99 Ms

latency_budget_hard_ms.description: Absolute ceiling. Regions above it are eliminated.
latency_budget_hard_ms.title: Latency Budget Hard Ms

DemandSource.title: DemandSource

Flow.description:
A WAF flow: a sequence of actions across components that performs a
function, carrying its own criticality, recovery targets, and constraints.

This is where resiliency and latency requirements actually live, because
that is where the business states them — a checkout flow and a nightly
reporting flow in the same workload have genuinely different RTOs.

path.description: Component names, in order. A user flow starts at its entry point.
path.title: Path

compliance.description: Compliance scope carried by this flow, e.g. ['pci-dss']. Inherited by its path.
compliance.title: Compliance

residency.description: Residency envelope carried by this flow. Inherited by its path.

origins.description: For user flows: which demand origins drive it, by `demand[].geography`. Empty means all of them.
origins.title: Origins

data_volume_gb_month.description: Approximate data moved along this path per month. Used to price the egress penalty when a flow has to be split across regions.
data_volume_gb_month.title: Data Volume Gb Month

splittable.description: False forbids the engine from placing this flow's components in different regions, whatever the latency maths says.
splittable.title: Splittable

Flow.title: Flow

FlowType.description:
WAF distinguishes the two; they score differently.

A user flow's latency is measured from a demand origin; a system flow's is
measured between components.
FlowType.title: FlowType

LandingZone.description:
The customer's existing estate. CAF's landing-zone region guidance treats
adding a region as real work — a new hub or vWAN hub in the Connectivity
subscription, gateways, DNS forwarders, identity expansion, workspace
placement. That cost is scored, not assumed away.

context.description: Path to a tenant context JSON, or 'live' to collect from ARM.
context.title: Context

LandingZone.title: LandingZone

Priorities.description:
Weights for ranking the regions that survive the hard filters.

Each maps to a criterion CAF names in 'Select Azure regions'. CAF prescribes
the criteria and their sequence but not a ranking method, so the weighting
is ours — and the decision record says so rather than implying Microsoft
prescribed it.

Sustainability is deliberately absent: it appears nowhere in CAF's region
guidance.

latency.description: CAF: choose regions close to your users.
latency.title: Latency

capacity_confidence.description: CAF: plan for capacity constraints. Proven restrictions eliminate a region outright; this weight covers the inferred signals.
capacity_confidence.title: Capacity Confidence

region_category.description: Azure's own Recommended vs Alternate classification — broadest service coverage and AZ support.
region_category.title: Region Category

landing_zone_expansion.description: Cost of standing up platform footprint in a new region.
landing_zone_expansion.title: Landing Zone Expansion

Priorities.title: Priorities

Residency.description:
Hard containment rules. Declarable at three levels — workload (the
default), flow (inherited by every component on the path), and component
(an explicit override). The engine resolves a component's effective envelope
as the intersection of all three.

jurisdictions.description: Jurisdiction codes the data must stay inside, e.g. ['eu'], ['de'].
jurisdictions.title: Jurisdictions

allowed_regions.description: Explicit whitelist — nothing outside it is ever a candidate. Usually populated from the landing zone's allowedLocations policy assignment rather than by hand.
allowed_regions.title: Allowed Regions

Residency.title: Residency

ResiliencyConstraints.description:
Constraints on *how* the engine may satisfy flow recovery targets.

Note this holds no topology field — topology is derived per component from
flow RTO/RPO. What lives here is the boundary the engine must work inside.

require_paired_region.description: Force the secondary to be the Azure-designated paired region. Off by default: CAF now states that favouring paired regions is 'no longer mandatory' and that regions should be chosen on latency, compliance and resiliency needs. Set this only for a service that genuinely depends on pairing, or a standing customer mandate.
require_paired_region.title: Require Paired Region

max_regions.description: Cap on total regions, e.g. to bound operational surface.
max_regions.title: Max Regions

ResiliencyConstraints.title: ResiliencyConstraints

Topology.description:
Normally an engine *output*, derived from flow RTO/RPO.

Accepted as an input only as an override, for cases where a customer has a
standing mandate rather than a requirement.
Topology.title: Topology

compliance.description: Workload-wide compliance scope, e.g. ['iso-27001']. Flows may add their own.
compliance.title: Compliance

flows.description: WAF flow inventory. If empty, one implicit flow spanning every component is assumed — see `effective_flows()`.
flows.title: Flows

horizon.description: Planning window for capacity and cost, e.g. '24mo'. Without it the decision is point-in-time.
horizon.title: Horizon
